title: The Mostowski collapse: representing well-founded relations by membership

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 30–31 (§6, Theorem 6.6, Definition 6.10, and Theorem 6.11; restricted here to set-sized carriers)

summary: A well-founded extensional relation on a set has a unique representation as membership on a transitive set.
abstract: A well-order can be replaced by an ordinal without changing which points precede which. The Mostowski collapse extends this idea to relations on sets that need not be orders. It requires two conditions: every nonempty subset has a point with no predecessor in that subset, and different points have different sets of predecessors. Under these conditions, each point can be replaced uniquely by a set whose members represent exactly its predecessors. The resulting sets form a transitive set, meaning that all their members are included in the representation, and no information about the original relation is lost.
